body:
Bounded follow-up finding from the SupportAssessment portable gate; not part of bd-01M19956MFSG7076QE4J66T7E9.

On exact candidate 6a218927a3492e27d34915aed4bcbf269bb004e7, support shares are now byte-stable across JVM, Scala.js, and Scala Native after deterministic sorted eligible-term summation. Fresh WOG HSMM inference itself still differs on Native in two least-significant bits outside support:

- one transition-flow value is 0x3f1b6b38f0f1bc5f on Native versus 0x3f1b6b38f0f1bc60 on JVM/JS;
- one posterior value is 0x3f655be4582d2fe5 on Native versus 0x3f655be4582d2fe4 on JVM/JS.

Consequently Native's fresh hsmm/v4 encoding has SHA-256 ff85950f19a8fff5d2e5ba7dc22c4fb9f77db660fbc64deca4d00ead9ce1b1e9 rather than the committed JVM/JS resource hash. Decode/re-encode remains canonical on Native, and the full Native align/codec/fixtures/laws courts pass; the current portable golden court therefore skips only fresh-inference byte/checksum equality on Native and says so in source.

This is a separate numerical-reproducibility question in existing HSMM arithmetic. It does not justify widening the support-honesty candidate, and it should not be silently treated as cross-platform byte identity. Please route to a new bead for exact-stage localization and a decision on whether the scientific contract requires bit identity or a named tolerance/receipt distinction.
